why: One axis, built deep: vampires enter -> tokens appear -> tokens convert into value -> drain closes. From captain's log 002 and the deck audit, which agree: card-advantage 4 v target 10, ramp 7 v 10-12, interaction 12 v target 5-6 and never castable. CUTS the anthem/+1+1/pump package and the Edgar attack plan (a six-drop whose payoff needs a board that survived, which this pod does not sell), plus 3 interaction slots the deck could never afford to hold up. ADDS the drain shell, sacrifice outlets and converters, and bodies that replace themselves. VAMPIRE-FIRST where the job is the same: eminence only mints a token when you cast a Vampire, so Scion of Opulence beats Pitiless Plunderer and Acolyte of Aclazotz beats a generic outlet. Ten of the seventeen adds are Vampires; seven came out of the Atlas library.

staged.why: The spell refactor moved the pips underneath the manabase: B short by 7, R by 5, W by 1. A Plains is one source; Exotic Orchard is all three at once and untapped.
Swamp is one source. Path of Ancestry is all three, and its scry fires on every Vampire cast — 40+ of them here, so it is card selection as well as fixing. Costs a turn.
B+R untapped while two Swamps remain. R is the scarcer of the two after the refactor.
Minas Tirith is a conditional-tapped W-only source. Phyrexian Tower is an untapped B source AND a free sacrifice outlet, which is the axis this branch is built on.
